core_obligations: Reduce the absolute assertions (1) and (2) to the relative assertions (3) and (4) over B = Spec(Z) (proof lines 1790-1794).
Build the commutative square of diagonals over B and show that the right vertical arrow is universally closed, hence quasi-compact (proof lines 1795-1807).

Assume Delta_{X/B} quasi-compact and verify the quasi-compactness of Delta_{Y/B} on quasi-compact Z over Y x_B Y through the base changed surjective morphism with quasi-compact source (proof lines 1810-1815).
Assume Delta_{X/B} a closed immersion and conclude that Delta_{Y/B} is universally closed by the same base change test (proof lines 1818-1822).
Combine representability, local finite typeness and monomorphismhood of the diagonal with universal closedness to obtain a closed immersion, hence separatedness of Y over B (proof lines 1823-1832).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its four assertions: for a surjective universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a base B, quasi-separatedness and separatedness of X (over B, and absolutely) pass to Y (source lines 1777-1788). The proof is a diagram chase on the squares of diagonals Delta_{X/B} and Delta_{Y/B}: the right vertical arrow X x_B X -> Y x_B Y is universally closed as a composite of universally closed morphisms and therefore quasi-compact, which converts quasi-compactness of Delta_{X/B} into quasi-compactness of Delta_{Y/B} by testing on quasi-compact Z over Y x_B Y, and converts the closed immersion property of Delta_{X/B} into universal closedness of Delta_{Y/B}; the last step then uses that the diagonal of a morphism of algebraic spaces is representable, locally of finite type and a monomorphism to upgrade universally closed to a closed immersion.
